## The Problem

You fit a model to your data. Great! Is it ready to use IRL?
who knows
But how useful is it against new data?
How can we evaluate?
resampling methods - cross validation

- Chapter 2: Test error rate is the average error resulting from using a statistical learning method to predict response on new observation, not in the training set
- What if test error cannot be easily calculated, and a designated test set is not available?
- The training error can easily be calculated by applying statistical learning methods to training data
- training error rate can be very different from test error rate, where the format canunderestimate the other

## The Solution (one of them, anyway)
- So if no test set is available to directly estimate the test error rate, then how can be estimat this quantity with the available training data?
- Many methods, but in this one, will think about HOLDING out a subset of the training data from itting procedss then applying learning method to those observations

## Validation Set Approach

Randomly divide the training data or avaialble ser of observations into 2 parts
- Training set: fit the model using this data
- Use fitted model to predict responses for observatiosn in validation set
- Validation set or hold-out set:resulting validation set error rate typ assessing using MSE in cae of quantitative response to estimate test error rate

## Comparison of 2 models
- ch 3:look at p-values of 2 coefficients
- CONS:
- Here, use validation sets. validation set MSE for cubic fit slightly than for quadratic fit
- right panel - validation est error can be variable
- in validation approach - methods tend to perform worse trained on fewer obs

## Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation

$CV_{(n)} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} MSE_{i}$

## LOOCV advantages over validation set
- far less bias
- training sets with n-1 oserations,

$CV_{(n)} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left( \frac{y_i - \hat{y_i}}{1-h_i} \right)$
- \hat{y}_i: ith fitted value from original least squares fit
- \hat{h}_i leverage defined in 3.37 in 99
- leverage lies between $\frac{1}{n}$ and 1, reflecting amount observation influences its own fit.
- good for any kind fo predictive modeling


## k-fold Cross Validation

-Alternative to LOOCV is k-fold CV
- randomly divide set of observations, first told treated as validaition set and method on remaining $k-1$ folds. 
- $MSE_1$ comptered on obs on the held out fold\
- repeat process k times
- each time, different group of obs treated as validation set
- k estimates of test error
- average MSEs

$CV_{(k)} = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{i=1}^{k} MSE_{i}$

- LOOCV is special case of k-fold CV where k is set to equal n.
- Computational advantage

## Real vs. simulated data
- real data, don't know true test MSE so hard to see accuracy of cross validation estimate
- simulated data - compute true test MSE, evalute accuracy of cross-vaildaiotion 
- Only intersted in location of minium point in estimtted test MSE curve,
- perfomring cross-validation on many learning methods, or single method wit hdifferent levels of flexibility to ID methods resulting in lowest test error
